classification.difficultyReason: Construct two short proofs of rectangle tests using angle properties, the quadrilateral angle sum and the rectangle definition.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that: A parallelogram with one right angle is a rectangle.

answer.short: The adjacent angles are supplementary to the right angle, so they are also $90^\circ$. The remaining angle is $90^\circ$ by the quadrilateral angle sum. Hence the parallelogram is a rectangle.
answer.worked:
Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with $\angle ABC=90^\circ$.
Since $AB\parallel CD$, co-interior angles give
$$\begin{align*}\angle BCD&=180^\circ-90^\circ\\\angle BCD&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Since $AD\parallel BC$, co-interior angles also give $\angle DAB=90^\circ$.
Using the angle sum of a quadrilateral,
$$\begin{align*}\angle CDA&=360^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ\\\angle CDA&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
All interior angles of the parallelogram are right angles, so $ABCD$ is a rectangle.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Prove that: If all angles of a quadrilateral are equal, then the quadrilateral is a rectangle.

answer.short: Each angle is $360^\circ\div4=90^\circ$. Supplementary co-interior angles show that both pairs of opposite sides are parallel. Thus the quadrilateral is a parallelogram with four right angles, so it is a rectangle.
answer.worked:
Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with all four interior angles equal. The angle sum of a quadrilateral gives
$$\begin{align*}\angle DAB&=360^\circ\div4\\\angle DAB&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Therefore every interior angle is $90^\circ$.
Since $\angle DAB+\angle ABC=180^\circ$, the converse co-interior angle test gives $AD\parallel BC$.
Since $\angle ABC+\angle BCD=180^\circ$, the same test gives $AB\parallel CD$.
Thus $ABCD$ is a parallelogram whose interior angles are right angles, so it is a rectangle.
